automation_name: AI Security Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.date_rule: Only a source with an unambiguous publication or update timestamp inside this window qualifies. Date-only and boundary-only claims are excluded.

searched_topics: agent and tool security including MCP and browser agents
source_method: Public-web collection using official vendor security advisories, the NVD CVE API, a vendor incident report, and an official security-research post. No private, local, or sensitive repository content was sent to an external service.

qualifying_findings.title: Opera Neon MCP Hub browser-agent channel verification flaw
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD record with vendor security-advisory reference
qualifying_findings.summary: CVE-2026-123139 says Opera Neon MCP Hub extension 0.0.1 on macOS and Windows did not verify a communication-channel source, allowing a malicious installed extension to send commands through MCP Hub to the built-in Browser Operator.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Opera Neon MCP Hub extension 0.0.1; macOS and Windows.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An extension crossing into the browser agent's action channel can inherit agentic browser authority; extension-to-agent origin binding is a distinct delegated-authority boundary.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad Opera product coverage; retain this security-specific browser-agent trust-boundary finding locally.
qualifying_findings.confidence: High for disclosure and affected component; consult the vendor advisory for remediation details before synthesis.
follow_up_actions: Verify the vendor remediation and fixed build
Audit installed extensions and Browser Operator channel exposure

qualifying_findings.title: SakanaAI text-to-LoRA checkpoint-loader path traversal
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD record, CNA-referenced project issue, and public proof-of-concept reference
qualifying_findings.summary: CVE-2026-126996 reports that text-to-LoRA 0.0.1 passes an attacker-controlled base_model_name_or_path into get_tokenizer during checkpoint loading, permitting path traversal; NVD notes public exploit disclosure and no project response at publication.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: SakanaAI text-to-LoRA 0.0.1 checkpoint loading; no fixed version stated.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model and checkpoint loading are supply-chain boundaries; untrusted path input can escape the intended model-artifact namespace.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns the broad project/entity; retain the model-artifact loading security implication locally.
qualifying_findings.confidence: Medium: NVD and the referenced public issue support the disclosure, while maintainer confirmation and a fix are absent.
follow_up_actions: Verify the reproducer against the referenced revision
Check for a maintainer patch or security advisory before durable synthesis

qualifying_findings.title: MLflow FileStore model_id path traversal fixed in 3.18.0
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD record with upstream commit and release references
qualifying_findings.summary: CVE-2026-127202 reports that MLflow before 3.18.0 with FileStore could accept ../ sequences in model_id on the log outputs API, enabling unauthenticated writes outside a run directory within the service account's permissions.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: MLflow before 3.18.0 using FileStore; FileStore was default before 3.7.0 and later opt-in through MLFLOW_ALLOW_FILE_STORE.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model-tracking and artifact services are AI deployment supply-chain surfaces; traversal can alter host-side state beyond the intended experiment/run boundary.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad MLflow coverage; retain this fixed tracking-service security delta locally.
qualifying_findings.confidence: High: NVD cites upstream commit and 3.18.0 release.
follow_up_actions: Upgrade FileStore-backed MLflow deployments to 3.18.0 or later
Review exposed log-outputs API and service-account write scope

qualifying_findings.title: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server v1.1.0 closes SQL and approval-boundary flaws
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD records with GitHub Security Advisory, upstream commit, pull-request, and release references
qualifying_findings.summary: Before 1.1.0, the server's read_only path could use PostgreSQL simple-query execution for unrecognized statements (CVE-2026-126196); custom pl-do tools could interpolate attacker input into DO blocks (CVE-2026-126197); and bundled clients based write confirmation on a tool name instead of write annotations (CVE-2026-126198).
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server before 1.1.0; CVE-2026-126198 is a bundled-client confirmation control, not a server authorization boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP-to-database integrations must enforce least privilege and server-side authorization independently of client confirmation or model behavior.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad pgEdge/MCP product coverage; retain the database delegated-action security controls locally.
qualifying_findings.confidence: High: NVD details and upstream v1.1.0 references agree; validate advisory remediation notes during synthesis.
follow_up_actions: Treat database-role privileges and server authorization as primary controls
Confirm custom tools carry accurate write annotations

qualifying_findings.title: Unit 42 reports autonomous Cairn intrusion operations
qualifying_findings.summary: Unit 42 reports that Chinese-speaking attackers paired the open-source Cairn penetration-testing framework with Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek models for 25 autonomous operations against at least 19 organizations in August-September 2026, obtaining unauthorized access or data at 10; Unit 42 tracks the activity as CL-STA-1238 with moderate confidence.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Autonomous target-to-action workflow using a modified/open-source AI penetration-testing framework; no software version is a remediation target.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The report is a public incident illustrating how model-enabled planning and tool execution can scale intrusion activity, reinforcing action logging, credential isolation, and approval/egress controls.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad framework/model entities; retain the incident and its security controls locally.
qualifying_findings.confidence: Medium-high: a primary vendor report, but attribution and operational totals are Unit 42 assessments.
follow_up_actions: Use the report's indicators and defensive guidance only after reviewing the original report

qualifying_findings.title: Jet Admin Cloud Platform prompt injection disclosure
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD/CVE record with CISA CSAF reference
qualifying_findings.summary: CVE-2026-123965 states that a free-account attacker could use prompt injection in Jet Admin Cloud Platform to expose .env configuration files and exfiltrate credentials; the record says the issue was mitigated via a sandbox component around October 29, 2026.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: All versions are stated as affected; the record names a sandbox mitigation but does not give a release version.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Prompt-injection resistance must include containment for secret-bearing execution environments, not only prompt-layer filtering.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns the broad product entity if needed; retain the prompt-injection and secret-exfiltration lesson locally.
qualifying_findings.confidence: Medium: official vulnerability record supports the fact, but vendor remediation/version evidence should be checked before synthesis.
follow_up_actions: Verify the vendor changelog or advisory
Confirm sandbox coverage and rotate potentially exposed credentials

qualifying_findings.title: ragent RAG traces authorization and knowledge-document XSS disclosures
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD records with public source-code and project-issue references
qualifying_findings.summary: CVE-2026-129157 says ragent 1.0.0-1.1.0 let any logged-in user read other users' RAG traces, including identities, questions, and execution details. CVE-2026-129158 says ragent 1.1.0 served uploaded SVG knowledge-base documents inline, allowing authenticated stored XSS and potential account takeover.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ragent 1.0.0-1.1.0 for trace authorization; ragent 1.1.0 for SVG document upload/rendering.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: RAG observability data is sensitive cross-tenant content, and knowledge-base ingestion/rendering is both a document-trust and browser-session boundary.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad ragent/RAG entity coverage; retain the local data-isolation and content-rendering security implications.
qualifying_findings.confidence: Medium-high: NVD includes code and issue references; no maintainer fix is established in the inspected evidence.
follow_up_actions: Verify fixed versions with the project
Apply per-tenant authorization checks to trace APIs
Treat uploaded SVG as active content or force safe download

qualifying_findings.title: IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway multi-boundary advisory set
qualifying_findings.visible_date: 2026-11-13T22:17:20Z (NVD publications; 17:17 local time, within the window)
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD records referencing IBM PSIRT advisories
qualifying_findings.summary: The in-window IBM advisory set covers cross-tenant bulk-import overwrite of tool/resource/prompt endpoints and credentials (CVE-2026-110178); filter-guard and schema-regex denial of service (CVE-2026-110189, CVE-2026-94407); SSRF (CVE-2026-110194); token-exchange cache and upstream-authorization credential isolation failures (CVE-2026-110195, CVE-2026-110279); and identity-claim replay/exposure to third-party MCP servers (CVE-2026-110278).
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ContextForge MCP Gateway 1.0.0-1.0.11, with selected findings also affecting 1.1.0; consult each IBM PSIRT advisory for the exact fixed release.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A gateway concentrates delegated tools, tenant data, upstream credentials, and identity claims; each requires independent tenant, origin, cache-key, and availability controls.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad ContextForge/MCP entity coverage; retain this security-specific multi-tenant and delegated-credential advisory set locally.
qualifying_findings.confidence: High for the CVE facts and affected ranges; fixed-version information requires direct IBM PSIRT review.
follow_up_actions: Review all linked IBM PSIRT advisories
Audit imported public tool resources, cached token exchanges, upstream authorization headers, identity propagation, and gateway resource limits
